collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A villager who speaks two languages must translate a tense negotiation: translate exactly, or soften the angry words.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) grew up speaking both Isola's language and the language of the island across the bay, and today (subject.he/she) must translate between the two villages' elders over a fishing dispute. One elder from across the bay has just said something very rude. (friend), from the village, is waiting for the translation. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) translates it exactly. (friend) goes red. There is shouting. Then, slowly, the two sides get to what they actually mean, and the dispute is settled by sunset. Honesty, it turns out, is faster.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) softens it into something polite. The talks go smoothly, and an agreement is made. Later, (friend) learns what was really said, and is uncomfortable that (subject) chose for (friend.him/her). (subject) says (subject.he/she) only kept the peace.
